In 1932, Caltech physicist Carl Anderson discovered the positron, the first particle of antimatter to be identified. Anderson had not set out to hunt antimatter.

He had built a cloud chamber to determine the composition of cosmic rays, high-energy particles that rain down from space.

The instrument included a magnet, which allowed Anderson to determine whether particles passing through were positively or negatively charged, and a lead plate to slow the particles down.

Anderson took hundreds of photographs of tracks taken by cosmic ray particles, but he was stymied by tracks like the one in this post.

The curve of the trajectory suggested the particle was positively charged yet far less massive than a proton.

An editor at the journal Physical Review suggested the name positron, since the particle resembled a positively charged electron.

Only later did Anderson realize that the positron was identical to the electron except for the opposite charge - Paul Dirac had predicted the existence of such an antiparticle in 1931.

Anderson was awarded the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery.

The removal of the "to be" verb ("been" in the given sentence) and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)

For example:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1 is 'challenge'. The passage talks about riddles, describing them as captivating enigmas that engage our minds and ignite our imagination. Riddles prompt us to think creatively and solve mysteries using wit and logic. The given sentence indicates that riddles serve a purpose - they encourage us to think creatively and solve mysteries. The word that best fits this purpose is "challenge." Riddles present a mental challenge or puzzle that engages our minds and requires creative thinking to solve. "Challenge" is the word that aligns most logically with the context of the passage.

Riddles aren't meant to 'inhibit' (to hinder, restrain, or prevent something from happening or developing), 'destroy' (to damage something severely or completely, rendering it unusable or non-existent), or 'dissolve' (to become weaker, break apart, or disappear gradually) anything; instead, they stimulate our minds by presenting intellectual challenges.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2 is 'forms'. The sentence discusses riddles and their diverse nature. It mentions that riddles come in various types or varieties. Among the options provided, "forms" is the word that most aptly describes the different types or varieties that riddles can take. Riddles can come in different forms or formats, such as ancient folklore, modern brain teasers, or other variations.

'Structures' signifies the underlying framework or design of something. While riddles might have a structure or format in terms of their presentation or how they are constructed, this word doesn't convey the diversity or variety of riddles mentioned in the passage. It doesn't encompass the range of different types or categories that riddles can come in.

'Seasons' refers to the different periods of the year and doesn't relate to the varied types or categories of riddles mentioned in the passage.

'Resolutions' refers to solutions, outcomes, or decisions reached after resolving a problem or situation. In the context of riddles, this word doesn't fit as it doesn't describe the various types or categories of riddles themselves but rather the outcome of solving them.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3 is 'chase'. In the given context, "chase" (a hunt or a search, especially in a determined or persistent manner) implies that engaging with riddles involves actively pursuing or chasing the solutions. It suggests the idea of actively seeking answers or solutions to the riddles, engaging in a mental chase to unlock the answers. Other words are not suitable for the blank.

'Hesitation' refers to a moment of pausing or indecision before taking action.

'Sedation' refers to the act of calming or inducing a state of calmness or relaxation. It doesn't fit the context of the passage, which discusses the mental stimulation and excitement derived from engaging with riddles.

'Turmoil' refers to a state of confusion, disturbance, or disorder. While it represents an intense state of chaos or unrest, it doesn't reflect the positive and intellectually stimulating nature of engaging with riddles.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4 is 'approach'. The sentence talks about engaging with riddles, encouraging the reader to approach/handle/tackle problems from unconventional angles. In the context of riddles, "approach" signifies the mindset or perspective taken while trying to unravel the mysteries presented by the riddles. It involves the mental attitude, methods, or tactics used to tackle the challenge of understanding and solving these enigmatic puzzles. In the given sentence, "approach" suggests the need to adopt different, perhaps unconventional, perspectives or ways of thinking when engaging with riddles to successfully find their solutions.

'Depart' means to leave or move away from a particular place or situation. In the context of solving riddles, using "depart" doesn't fit the intended meaning of the sentence. The sentence emphasises the active involvement and mental engagement required in approaching riddles, rather than moving away from them.

"Evade" means to avoid or escape from something, typically by using cleverness or trickery. In the given context, using "evade" doesn't align with the idea of actively engaging with riddles. Instead, it suggests avoiding or sidestepping the challenges presented by the riddles, which contradicts the intended meaning of the sentence.

'Disregard' means to pay no attention to something or to ignore it. This word doesn't match the context of the sentence, which emphasises the active mental involvement and creative problem-solving needed to approach riddles.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The most suitable option to fill in blank number 5 is 'invite'. In the given context, the word that best fits is 'invite' as it conveys the idea that riddles draw or welcome people into a world filled with mystery and intrigue. It suggests that solving these puzzles offers an invitation to enter this engaging and enigmatic realm. The word "invite" aligns with the notion that engaging with riddles introduces individuals to a captivating and intellectually stimulating experience. Other words do not fit the context of the sentence.

'Repel' means to drive away or cause someone to feel aversion or dislike towards something. "Resist" means to withstand or oppose something.

In this context, using "resist" doesn't align with the intended meaning of the sentence. It implies that individuals are actively fighting against or trying to avoid entering the world of mystery and intrigue presented by riddles. However, the sentence conveys the idea that engaging with riddles is inviting and intriguing rather than something to resist.

'Follow' means to go or come after or behind someone or something. This word doesn't suit the context of the sentence. It implies a passive action of simply trailing behind or imitating something. However, the sentence is describing how riddles immerse individuals into a fascinating and enigmatic world, rather than suggesting a literal following or mimicry.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

Has Rohit written the letter? (Active)

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Despite its global reach, the Great Recession's effects were particularly pronounced in these regions. B. It caused a significant increase in home mortgage foreclosures, leaving millions of people without their life savings, jobs, and homes. C. The crisis originated from the subprime mortgage crisis, with the United States and Western Europe experiencing the most severe consequences. D. The Great Recession, a global economic downturn, wreaked havoc on financial markets, banking, and real estate industries worldwide.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Despite its global reach, the Great Recession's effects were particularly pronounced in these regions.

B. It caused a significant increase in home mortgage foreclosures, leaving millions of people without their life savings, jobs, and homes.

C. The crisis originated from the subprime mortgage crisis, with the United States and Western Europe experiencing the most severe consequences.

D. The Great Recession, a global economic downturn, wreaked havoc on financial markets, banking, and real estate industries worldwide.
questions.solution: The correct order to form a coherent paragraph is DBCA. Sentence D comes first as it introduces the topic of the Great Recession and its global impact and provides context for the subsequent sentences. Sentence B comes next as it provides specific information about one of the consequences of the recession, which is an increase in home mortgage foreclosures, highlighting the severity of its impact on individuals. Sentence C then provides the origin of the crisis and emphasises the severity of its impact on the United States and Western Europe. Lastly, sentence A concludes the paragraph by highlighting the disproportionate impact of the Great Recession on certain regions, despite its global nature. The term 'these regions' in sentence A refers to the United States and Western Europe (introduced in sentence C). Accordingly, CA forms a necessary pair. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
To express a sentence in the future tense, we need to use the future tense form of the verbs. In English, the future tense is often formed using the auxiliary verb "will", followed by the base form of the main verb. To convert this sentence to the future tense, we need to change the verb "are" to its future tense form. The future tense of "are" is "will be." Option (a) correctly uses the future tense ("will be") to express the idea of the original sentence. Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note: Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are: be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, will is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb sing.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The sovereign's title will be taking away from them for misgovernment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The sovereign's title will be taking away from them for misgovernment.
questions.solution:
The underlined part of the sentence is in active voice. The verb 'taking' is acting on the object but it should act on the subject 'title' for the sentence to be meaningful. So, the underlined part should be in passive voice. So, the underlined part of the sentence is incorrect. Option (d) is also in active voice. So, it is also eliminated. 'Took' is the past tense of the verb 'take'. We use the past/present participle of a verb after the verb 'be'. So, option (a) is incorrect. Option (c) is in passive voice and 'taken' is past participle. Among the given options, option (c) is the most appropriate choice.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Voice of a sentence - Depending upon the emphasis we want to lay we use a particular voice in a particular context. We use active voice to lay emphasis on the doer of the action while we use passive voice to lay emphasis on the receiver of the action.

Example:

Active- Radha will work. (emphasis on Radha)

Passive- Work will be done by Radha. (emphasis on Work)

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Despite the persistent challenges posed of / economic downturns, technological advancements / continue to reshape industries and / redefine business landscapes.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the persistent challenges posed of / economic downturns, technological advancements / continue to reshape industries and / redefine business landscapes.

options.text: Despite the persistent challenges posed of
options.html: Despite the persistent challenges posed of

questions.solution:
The verb 'posed' should be followed by 'by', and not 'of' to denote what poses the challenges.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

The correct sentence is: Despite the persistent challenges posed by economic downturns, technological advancements continue to reshape industries and redefine business landscapes.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who walks on ropes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who walks on ropes.
questions.solution: 'Somnambulist' means a person who suffers from somnambulism (a condition in which a person walks around while they are sleeping); 'funambulist' means one who walks on ropes; 'ambulift' means a special vehicle for transporting persons with reduced mobility, wheelchairs, stretchers, etc. for boarding airplanes; 'ambulant' means (of a patient) able to walk about. Hence, b) is the correct answer.
